data.long_meaning: From the Latin norus meaning 'honour, light'. Norina is a variant of the Latin name Norina, which was derived from the Roman goddess Norus, representing the north wind. The name Norina carries the meaning “Light, Honour” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Norina usually hope their child will grow to embody light, honour and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Norina total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: In the 4th century AD, a saint named Norina is believed to have lived and performed miracles in the region of Pannonia, now part of modern-day Hungary. She was a virgin who was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian. Her relics were later enshrined in the city of Szombathely.

During the Middle Ages, there is a legend of a Christian girl named Norina, who was born in the town of Montemarciano, Italy. She is said to have been blessed with the gift of healing and was able to cure many sick people in the region. Her name became associated with the Madonna and Child, and she was venerated as a saint in local folklore.
